When a check made on its own (at start and once a day) finds a new version, it is downloaded, checked (SHA256) and installed. If Android asks for confirmation, a notification lets you know. Update now installs a version found by Check now either way.
Version %s is ready: confirm the install in Android\'s prompt
Version %s did not match its SHA256 checksum, so it was not installed
New version ready to install — tap to install
Bugs, errors, ideas — anything. Your mail app opens with the app version, device and recent log filled in.

Rest the mouse pointer against an edge of the screen for a moment and the group and the master mouse go to the channel set for that side. No network: each computer watches its own screen. Works while the master mouse is on this device.

To watch the screen edges flockswitch needs “Display over other apps”: thin invisible strips along the edges notice the pointer, and the countdown is drawn on top of what is on the screen. No input is taken.

Only a Logitech mouse with a haptic motor (currently the MX Master 4) vibrates. Test plays it once at the chosen strength while that mouse is on this device. The strength goes to the mouse when applied; the mouse forgets it when it loses power, so it is applied again whenever the mouse is here. “Options+” leaves the Logi Options+ setting alone.

The wait does not start until Control is down, even with the pointer at the edge. With flockswitch\'s accessibility service on, letting go calls it off at once; without it Android reports the key only as the pointer moves.
Turn on the accessibility service so the key counts even while the pointer rests.
Each effect keeps its own settings: choosing another effect shows its own.
A different effect each time, in that effect\'s own color and size. Where the effect has them, the direction and shrinking away are picked at random too.
When the mouse arrives from another computer

Android tells an app where the pointer is only through an accessibility service, and only by holding the mouse back from other apps while it listens. So flockswitch listens for just one event: the highlight appears at your next mouse movement, within 5 seconds, and stays where the pointer was then. The notification has a button for it too.
Find the cursor needs the accessibility service.
Android gives apps the mouse pointer\'s position only from Android 14 on. On this version only the preview can be shown.

Used only for flockswitch settings you turn on. Sees the keyboard to know whether Control is held and to catch Ctrl+Alt+L; every other key passes through untouched and nothing is stored or sent. Reads the mouse pointer\'s position once, at the next movement after you ask to find the cursor.
Puts every setting back to how it started.
Android tells an app about a keyboard\'s keys and the mouse pointer only through an accessibility service. The top and bottom edges, the Control option and Find the cursor need it.
It does not read the screen. It only looks at Control and Ctrl+Alt+L, and stores or sends nothing. You can turn it off on the same screen at any time.
1. Open the accessibility settings below, turn on flockswitch and allow it. On Samsung phones it is under \'Installed apps\'.
2. If a \'Restricted setting\' message appears, tap OK, open App info below, and choose \'Allow restricted settings\' from the ⋮ menu at the top right. Then do step 1 again.
3. Come back here to see below whether it is on.
2. Come back here to see below whether it is on.

flockswitch uses Android's accessibility service (AccessibilityService API) only for three optional features: switching at the top and bottom screen edges, “Only while Control is held”, and Find the cursor.

What it accesses
• Keys of a hardware keyboard: while “Only while Control is held” or the Ctrl+Alt+L shortcut is on, key presses pass through flockswitch. It only checks whether Control is held and takes Ctrl+Alt+L; every other key goes on to the app in front unchanged.
• The mouse pointer's position: read once, at your next mouse movement after you ask to find the cursor.
• Drawing on screen: invisible thin strips over the status and navigation bars notice the pointer at the top and bottom edges, and the Find the cursor highlight is drawn on top.
It does not read what is on the screen, and it does not record or keep the keys you type.

How it is used
Only on this device and only for these features. Nothing is stored, sent or shared, and this version of flockswitch has no internet access.

You can turn the service off at any time in Android's accessibility settings. With No thanks everything else keeps working and only these three features stay off; this notice opens again from “How to turn it on” or from Permissions on the General tab.
Needed to switch at the screen edge and to show effects.
Needed for the top and bottom edges, the Control option and Find the cursor.
The status and navigation bars cover the top and bottom edges, so those two need the accessibility service.

• Ctrl+Alt+L (find the cursor) is the only shortcut, and it cannot be changed. Left or right Ctrl and Alt both work; with Shift or the Meta key (Windows, ⌘ or Search) held too it does not count.
• “Only while Control is held” takes either Ctrl key.
• Only a hardware keyboard counts (USB, Bluetooth or on a receiver); the on-screen keyboard sends no keys.
• flockswitch's accessibility service must be on to see keys. Without it Ctrl+Alt+L does nothing, and Control is noticed only while the pointer moves.
• While it is on, Ctrl+Alt+L goes to flockswitch only, not to the app in front. Keys that Android or the device maker keep for themselves never reach flockswitch.
• The computers' channel shortcuts (Ctrl+Alt+1/2/3) do not exist on Android: use Switch now on the Home tab or the notification's channel buttons.

• flockswitch keeps a list of up to %1$d settings files it saved. When there are that many, delete some or tidy up in Manage before saving again.
• Manage lists them newest first: rename a file (it stays a .json file) or delete it from the device. A file deleted elsewhere drops off the list.
• A settings file can be copied to another Android phone or tablet (by cable, cloud storage, mail…) and loaded there with Load. Load opens any settings file, also one not on the list.
• Channels are per device: after loading on another device, check the channels on the Buttons tab.
• The computer versions keep their settings differently; their files cannot be loaded here.
